target.title: fix(cron): avoid ambiguous direct delivery retries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102367.

Cron direct delivery bypasses the durable outbound queue with `skipQueue: true`, but its local retry classifier still retried ambiguous transport errors such as `ECONNRESET` and generic gateway timeouts. Those errors can happen after Slack accepts or finalizes a message, so a retry can post the same scheduled announcement twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct cron retry path now reuses the outbound recovery proof predicate and retries only failures that prove no recipient-visible send happened, such as `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` or pre-connect network failures. Ambiguous send/finalization failures remain terminal for that cron delivery attempt so the operator sees the failure without risking a duplicate Slack post.

## User Impact

Scheduled Slack deliveries no longer retry ambiguous post-send transport failures that may already have delivered the message. Proven-not-sent failures still retry, preserving recovery for safe pre-dispatch failures.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` — first pass found the partial-batch retry gap; after the batch-level retry gate and regression test, rerun was clean with no accepted/actionable findings
- Testbox `tbx_01kxcs4xazjj962vcf4he56a44`: `corepack pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.double-announce.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.policy.test.ts` — 119 tests passed

Transcript not included: a local candidate was found, but publishing sanitized agent logs requires explicit maintainer approval.
